title: Universal homeomorphisms induce equivalences of small pro-etale topoi
statement:
Let $r:X\to Y$ be a universal homeomorphism of schemes [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. Use the small pro-etale sites with compatible size conventions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and the induced inverse and direct image adjunction $r^{-1}\dashv r_*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then these functors are quasi-inverse equivalences
$$
 r^{-1}:\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\mathrm{proet}})\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}}):r_*.
$$
In particular its unit $F\to r_*r^{-1}F$ and counit $r^{-1}r_*G\to G$ are isomorphisms for every sheaf of sets $F$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $G$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$.

source.place: Tag 09AB (proetale-lemma-thickening), with Tag 04DF (morphisms-lemma-universal-homeomorphism) identifying universal homeomorphisms with integral universally injective surjective morphisms.

proof.text: Apply direct-image topological invariance. Its specified adjunction gives the inverse-image equivalence and invertibility of every unit and counit component by the general adjunction equivalence API.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09AB; formal adjunction conclusion after the direct-image proof

split_report.summary: Expanded the Stacks affine ind-etale route in eight steps. Reused existing etale invariance, affineness descent, finite-presentation factorization and eventual equality, basis comparison, and localization nodes. Made the source's omitted covering check explicit and checked the actual unit and counit. No new nodes or statement corrections. The source Lean theorem contains sorry and addresses abelian-valued sheaves, so there is no attachment.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the opening site-equivalence paragraph of i-topology: its pro-etale counterpart is proved through affine ind-etale bases, then localized. No assertion that all weakly-etale objects descend as objects is needed; the derived and constructibility clauses belong to i-topology, not this item.

tool_uses.why: Affineness descent supplies matching affine opens and reflection of affine objects in the etale equivalence; this is a generic geometry tool, not a replacement for the unit topological-invariance route.
Finite-presentation compactness supplies the stage factorization in the ind-etale Hom formula; no node of this unit states this algebra tool.
Eventual vanishing with N=R proves equality of maps at a finite stage on finitely many generators.
Constructs the small filtered colimit of the diagram descended by the etale quasi-inverse.
Supplies weak etaleness of all arrows in the affine ind-etale basis.
Supplies the canonical set-sheaf localization comparisons used to return from affine pairs to general schemes.
Only clause (1), identification of the pro-etale site over an open object with the slice site, is used; it explicitly includes open immersions.
Generic adjunction lemma applied to opposite categories identifies the actual unit as an isomorphism.

I checked in tags/tags that 04DF, 04DZ, 05YU, 03CF and 04TQ name the cited labels. Statement: the universal-homeomorphism hypothesis equals 09AB's 'integral, universally injective, surjective' by 04DF, and the conclusion is the 09AB topos equivalence for sheaves of sets, with the canonical unit and counit. Nothing is added or weakened, and the parent uses it only for sets before its own module lift. Steps: step 1 checks the hypotheses of 05YU on matched affine opens. Step 2 is the etale equivalence restricted to affines, matching 05YX. Step 3: factorization gives surjectivity, and the tensor eventual-zero lemma with N=R gives injectivity. Step 4: full faithfulness from the ind-Hom formula, and essential surjectivity via the quasi-inverse applied to the whole diagram plus small colimits. Step 5: weakly etale arrows plus affine preimages give the fpqc condition, and the homeomorphic projections show joint surjectivity is preserved and reflected. Step 6: I checked every hypothesis of the dense-subsite theorem, including the covering-sieve criterion, which holds by fullness, and that the square of restrictions is G(V_X). Step 7: opposite-adjunction argument, then the triangle identity and full faithfulness. Step 8: slice identification (clause 1), 03CF comparisons, unit and counit compatibility from the section formulas, and gluing over a Zariski cover with isIso_of_coversTop. Edge cases checked: empty scheme, identity, purely inseparable field extension, integral but non-finite maps, non-quasi-separated schemes. Duplicate search: rg for 09AB and for universal homeomorphism with pro-etale; the only related node, a condensed closed-surjective-immersion result, is narrower and not a duplicate. review_split PASS, no undeclared route departures; I accept the eight declared tool_uses as generic tools. No SGA. Repair: step 5 only showed that u identifies the generated topologies, but step 6 cites clause (3) of lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-is-morphism-of-sites, which needs arbitrary, possibly infinite, families to match. I added the argument: a basis family over an affine V is a covering iff some finite subfamily is jointly surjective, and u preserves and reflects this. I also added def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis to step 5 uses; it was already in proof_deps. Corrected file: fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/lem-trf-proetale-topological-invariance.json. lean.statement: theorem proEtaleSheaf_topological_invariance {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (r : X ⟶ Y) (hr : (topologically IsHomeomorph).universally r) : (proEtaleSheafInverseImage r (Type (u + 1))).IsEquivalence ∧ (proEtaleSheafDirectImage r (Type (u + 1))).IsEquivalence ∧ (∀ F : Sheaf (ProEt.topology Y) (Type (u + 1)), IsIso ((proEtaleSheafAdjunction r (Type (u + 1))).unit.app F)) ∧ (∀ G : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) (Type (u + 1)), IsIso ((proEtaleSheafAdjunction r (Type (u + 1))).counit.app G))
